newsitem.title: USA: House to issue subpoenas in campaign finance probe.
newsitem.headline: House to issue subpoenas in campaign finance probe.

text.p: The top House investigator of campaign finance abuses said Wednesday that four key witnesses have refused to answer requests for documents and subpoenas will be issued to get them to comply.

Representative Dan Burton, an Indiana Republican who is chairman of the House Committee on Government Reform and Oversight, said the people involved are former Associate Attorney General Webster Hubbell, former Commerce Department official John Huang, former White House aide Mark Middleton and Charles Trie, an Arkansas businessman friend of President Clinton.

"I am disappointed that these individuals, some of whom were high ranking Clinton administration officials have declined to cooperate with the committee," Burton said in a statement. "The president has pledged full cooperation in this matter, and I would hope that the presidential appointees and friends would honour his commitment."
The committee so far has made more than 50 requests for documents to various people and government agencies, Burton said. These would be the first subpoenas.
On the Senate side, the Senate Governmental Affairs Committee has prepared more than 40 subpoenas for documents in connection with its investigation, Senate sources said.
Hubbell was in the final months of a 21-month prison sentence after pleading guilty to charges of defrauding his former law firm in Little Rock, Arkansas.

He reportedly also was under investigation by independent Whitewater counsel Kenneth Starr into how he became employed by the Lippo Group, an Indonesia-based financial group, after he left the Justice Department and whether his employment was an effort to restrict his cooperation in the Whitewater investigation.

Huang, a one-time Lippo official before moving to the Commerce Department and then becoming a top Democratic National Committee fundraiser last year, raised several million dollars for Democrats from Asian Americans and people with foreign ties.

Trie, an international business consultant, delivered more than $600,000 to Clinton's Whitewater legal defence fund but the money was returned after questions were raised about the origins of the funds.
Middleton was a businessman who reportedly raised funds in Asia for a foundation to help renovate Clinton's boyhood home in Arkansas.
